messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: p99 latency breach on prod-serving (us-west-2) detected 2026-03-15 09:12:47 UTC. Route affected: /v1/generate (streaming). Paging eng-oncall.

maria (oncall): got the page. Opening dashboards — p95 ~450ms -> up from normal, p99 ~2.3s. Streaming stalls around token ~150. Window 09:11-09:20 UTC. Any recent deploys?

kevin (sre): No deploys in that timeframe. Node CPU/GPU look normal, but kv metrics show eviction churn and fragmentation rising quickly. Prefill hit-rate dropped by ~40%.

sam (runtime): sounds like KV cache pressure + prefill/decode imbalance. When prefill fails we decode cold which explodes tail latency. Which pool is this?

maria (oncall): pool-4a is the one. Shard 12 shows heavy eviction and failed prefill attempts timing out.

kevin (sre): I can trigger an incremental compaction on shard 12 to reduce fragmentation. That may temporarily increase CPU. Alternative is to reroute traffic. Thoughts?

sam (runtime): Do incremental compaction first at low rate. Also disable prefill->decode fallback in pool-4a for short window to avoid adding decode pressure. And reduce prefix cache size for streaming to limit pressure.

maria (oncall): OK plan — 1) incremental compaction on pool-4a shard-12, 2) disable prefill->decode fallback for pool-4a, 3) set stream_prefix_cache_limit=8KB on pool-4a, 4) shift 10% traffic to pool-4b as a safety valve. Executing now.

kevin (sre): runbook ref: runbooks/kv-cache-pressure.md (compaction section). Command I'm about to run:

```
opsctl kv compaction start --shard=12 --mode=incremental --rate=0.2
```

maria (oncall): launching compaction job. Leaving console logs open.

ops-bot: compaction queued (job id comp-20260315-001). est runtime ~45s.

jess (support): FYI a customer (acme-corp) opened a ticket reporting slow streaming. I'll send a short interim update.

sam (runtime): while compaction runs I'll push config change to limit stream prefix caching:

```
cfgctl set pool-4a stream_prefix_cache_limit=8192 --reason="mitigation"
```

kevin (sre): compaction started. Monitoring eviction/sec and p99.

maria (oncall): compaction progress 60% — eviction rate dropping from ~120/s to ~35/s. p99 decreased to ~1.1s, p95 ~320ms. Streaming stalls still present but less frequent.

ops-bot: compaction comp-20260315-001 completed successfully (38s).

sam (runtime): applying cache-limit config now.

maria (oncall): initiating 10% reroute from pool-4a to pool-4b (canary) to absorb potential residual load.

kevin (sre): after reroute p99 ~820ms, p95 ~210ms. Prefill hit-rate improved to ~78% (was ~43%). Eviction normalized.

jess (support): sent message to affected customer: "We're mitigating elevated latency for streaming responses; engineers are working on it. Will follow up with root cause and ETA." Customer replied with :thumbsup:. Want an ETA to share?

maria (oncall): ETA ~30m for full stabilization. We're observing positive trends.

sam (runtime): immediate mitigation checklist for post-incident: - root cause: KV prefix churn causing fragmentation (hot prefixes + traffic fanout) - short-term: compaction + cache limit + reroute - medium-term: hotkey isolation, increase pool-4a cache allocation, adaptive prefill throttling, add safeties for prefill->decode fallback.

kevin (sre): I'll open INC-20260315-07 and schedule a 1-hour postmortem. Action items: alert on fragmentation_ratio > 0.35, autoscale cache shards when fragmentation > 0.4 && eviction_rate > 50/s, and test compaction impact during low-traffic windows.

maria (oncall): Handoff for next oncall: system stable, monitor for re-spike. Completed actions: compaction ran, stream_prefix_cache_limit=8KB applied, 10% reroute in place, prefill->decode fallback disabled on pool-4a. Prefill hit-rate improved to ~78%. Contacts: @sam, @kevin, @jess.

maria (oncall): reassigning follow-up to kevin for postmortem & mitigation backlog. Ending active pager but I'll stay on standby. Thanks all :heart:
